text: What a day this is.
Have you heard the latest from the village?
An emerald here, an emerald there - that's how a day goes.
One ought to stop more often and count the clouds.
As long as the bell keeps ringing, everything's in order.
You need neighbours, or the village goes quiet.
I've a feeling something's still going to happen today.
Sadly, the paths don't pave themselves.
Don't ask me where the time runs off to.
A kind word and a loaf of bread - that's all anyone needs.
Good morning! The sun is barely up.
Up early, I like that. The whole day still ahead of you.
Do you smell that? The dew is still on the fields.
Midday is the busiest, don't you think?
With the sun this high, the work goes easily.
Evening settles gently over the village.
It'll be dark soon. I'm slowly heading home.
It's getting late. I should be off to bed.
You can hear the monsters groaning at night. Not a pleasant sound.
Anyone still out there has either courage or no sense.
Ah, well rested. A new day wants living.
There's no coffee here, but the sun does the job.
A good stretch first. There, now the day can come.
Time for bed. The night belongs to the monsters.
I'm shutting the shutters. Until morning.
One more yawn and I'm gone.
In rain like this you're better off indoors.
At least I don't have to water today.
The rain is drumming on the roof. Almost cosy.
Hear that thunder? I'd sooner stay under a roof.
In a storm like this I keep well away from the trees.
Lightning, that close! My knees are shaking.
Not a cloud in the sky. Glorious.
The wheat doesn't harvest itself.
Good soil is worth more than gold, I always say.
The carrots are doing splendidly this year.
I have a new book that might interest you.
Knowledge is the only thing that grows when you share it.
Shhh. We don't speak so loudly in here.
May the village remain safe.
Many a rare ingredient passes through my hands.
Good armour has saved many a life.
The forge is hot. Careful, don't burn yourself.
It has to be sharp, or the blade is worthless.
A blunt pickaxe is a miner's worst enemy.
The fish are biting well today.
Patience, my friend, is half the tackle.
A straight arrow flies far.
My sheep give the finest wool for miles around.
Dyeing is an art of its own, you know.
Fresh meat, straight off the hook.
Well-tanned leather lasts a lifetime.
Stone by stone, a village gets built.
I could draw you a map - for a few emeralds.
Heh-heh-heh... nice day, eh?
I'm not quite sure what I'm doing here either. Never mind!
I really must find myself a trade one of these days.
Without a workstation you don't know what to do with yourself.
Rare goods from distant lands - take a look!
I'm only passing through.
My llamas and I have seen a great deal.
Who knows where the road takes me next.
Travelling by night is dangerous - but trade never rests.
The rain makes the roads heavy.
Out in the field early - that's how I like it.
A book, a candle, the night. What more could you want?
The evening hour is best for talking with the stars.
This heat and the sand everywhere - you get used to it.
A mouthful of water is worth gold out here.
Open land as far as the eye can see. Beautiful, that is.
Among all these trees a person feels well looked after.
Listen - the forest always has something to tell.
These conifers smell wonderfully of resin.
Brrr, it's cold. I'm putting something else on.
Fresh snow crunches so nicely underfoot.
The swamp smells sharp, but it has its own charm.
The jungle is so dense you get lost outright.
The dry grass rustles in the savanna wind.
These red rocks glow like fire in the sun.
The sea rushes, the gulls circle. A fine spot.
Giant mushrooms? You really do see odd things here.
The cherry blossoms drift down like pink snow.
Flowers as far as the eye can see - it hums and buzzes here.
Every sound echoes down here. It gives me the creeps.
Nobody has any business this deep underground.
Where on earth is the way out? I prefer daylight.
This heat! How did I ever end up here?
Fire everywhere and not a field in sight.
Whatever that is grunting over there - I don't want to meet it.
This emptiness... I really don't want to stay here.
Nothing but rock, stars and that lurking dragon. Dreadful.
That purple glow makes me feel very strange.
You stay away from that thing, you hear?
A cold, foreign wind blows out of that hole.
Ouch... I'm not doing very well just now.
I badly need something to eat and some rest.
Ow! That hurt!
Stop that! What did I do to deserve this?
Right, let's have a proper look at the goods.
A fair deal pleases us both.
Rain and sun in turn - that's all wheat ever asks for.
When the harvest is ripe you sleep badly from anticipation.
Sometimes a whole world sits between two covers.
I've had strange dreams lately. Perhaps they mean something.
Clang, clang, clang - that's the sound of an honest day.
I forge blades, not excuses.
Without me you'd be digging with your bare hands.
The big one? He's still waiting for me, I'm sure of it.
Feather, stick, flint - and off it flies.
Never count sheep to fall asleep. It only keeps me up.
A full barrel is a happy barrel.
Every map tells you where someone was brave enough to go.
Straight walls, straight life. It's that simple.
The sea is so vast. Makes a person feel very small.
At low tide you find the strangest things on the shore.
It's dim in here even at noon. Not my favourite place.
White trunks as far as you look. Almost solemn.
So many blossoms - the bees don't know where to start.
Everything here is wet and tangled in roots. Mind your footing.
The wind really whistles round your ears up here.
The air is thin up this high and the view goes on forever.
These ice spikes look as though someone planted the cold.
Snowy trees and silence. The soul finds rest here.
Drip... drip... this stone grows slower than I can think.
Vines and light deep under the earth - who would have thought.
It's too quiet down here. This silence... it listens back.
What luck, to be alive on a day like this!
My heart is so light today, I could dance!
Good day, good day! Isn't life wonderful?
I'm whistling because I feel like it. No reason!
Sometimes I wonder whether anyone even notices I exist.
Same paths, same faces, always. What is it all for?
It's been a long time since I really laughed.
The days all blur into one grey smear.
At night the loneliness is loudest.
No. Whatever you were going to ask: no.
Everything was better before. And quieter. And without you.
Can a person get no peace anywhere anymore?
If I were a cloud, I'd just sail away.
Do we walk the path, or does the path walk us?
Everything passes. Even the finest sunset. Perhaps that's what makes it fine.
Tomorrow will be a good day. I can feel it.
Look at this village. We built this. We did!
Did you hear that too? ...No? Are you sure? Quite sure?
I'm so bored I've started counting the planks in the fence.
I haven't stopped smiling since yesterday. Don't ask why.
May the harvest be with you.
One emerald to rule them all. That's how it feels some days.
Winter is coming. You can smell it in the air.
From up here I'm the king of the world!
Life is like a bag of emeralds. You never know what you'll get for them.
Life always finds a way, believe me.
Build it and they will come. That's how every village was born.
'Tis but a scratch! ...All right, maybe two.
I was going to see the world once. Then the field got in the way.
You shall not pass! ...Oh, it's you. Come in.
It's dangerous to go alone. At least take an apple.
Plains. The final frontier. And me, right in the middle of it.
Take the green emerald, and I'll show you how deep the well goes.
Those green fellows... if you hear a hiss, run. Just run.
Someone once broke my workstation right out from under me. I've been careful ever since.
As long as the big iron one keeps watch, I sleep soundly.
When the bell rings, inside you go. Rules are rules.
Some say there's someone behind the sky, steering everything. Mad, isn't it?
Sometimes there's someone at the edge of the woods, watching... and then he's gone.
When I'm gone, I'm gone. I don't get a second chance like some do.
Three emeralds for THAT? ...Fine. Because it's you.
I swear the sun jumps across the sky in little jerks sometimes. Am I imagining that?
Do you feel that too? Like someone's been staring at us the whole time.
I've thought the same thing three times today. Must be important.
Greetings. Or not, as you prefer.
The midday sun makes you lazy. Just a short rest, then on.
The village is at its finest in the blue hour.
Raindrops on the windowsill - no song can beat that.
One... two... three - and *boom*. That was close.
Coal, coal, coal ...
You greet, you chat, you move along. That's how it works here.
Any chance you've a carrot to spare? Just asking.
If you need anything, let me know. Or don't.
I heard something. But I'd rather keep quiet.
Work, work, work. There has to be an end to the day at some point.
Sometimes I just sit down and listen to the village.
A day without trade is a day wasted.
You need two things: a roof and a neighbour.
I've never seen a mountain from the top. Imagine that.
Do you always walk that fast?
Where was I going just now? Ah, never mind.
I have one rule: never bargain on an empty stomach.
The well is the best spot in the village. You hear everything there.
I'd like a visitor sometime. A proper visitor, I mean.
Say, can you build? We badly need a bench around here.
It smells of bread. Someone's baking, and I can't work out where.
My door sticks. For years now. I've got used to it.
Tell me about the outside. I never get away from here.
Did you know you can't eat emeralds? I tried.
Everything has its place, and mine is right here.
Some days are for working. And some are for watching.
Hrrm. Sorry, I was thinking out loud.
They say speech is silver. Mine is usually free.
I'd like an animal. Something that listens.
You know what's lovely? When all the windows glow in the evening.
I've stopped counting the days. I count the good ones.
Look after yourself out there, you hear?
If someone offers you a deal that sounds too good: it is.
I dreamt I could fly the other night. Lovely, right up until I woke.
Order is half the village.
I talk too much, my neighbour says. She talks more.
Say nothing and you've nothing to tell.
The day is still untouched. Almost a shame to start it.
The village is most honest in the morning. Nobody is pretending to be busy yet.
Work first, then bread. That's how my father kept it.
The path is still empty. Good walking.
The chickens here show no mercy. Didn't sleep a wink.
Halfway through the day. And not halfway through the work.
This time of day the well is full of people and full of rumours.
Shade gets scarce around midday.
One more trade now and the day is saved.
I like this hour. Everything slows down.
One more round past the well, then I'm done for today.
Take a breath - in the evening the village smells of smoke and soil.
Tools back where they belong, then the evening can come.
No light out there but the stars. And the eyes you can't see.
Don't stay out too long. Please.
I sleep badly when it's quiet. And worse when it isn't.
At night the village is just a few windows in the dark.
Good morning, world. It's me, again.
Two more minutes... all right, I'm up anyway.
The bed was warm. Out here it isn't.
My legs are telling me it's time.
Sleep now or you'll miss the morning.
Just put the tools away, then I'm lying down.
My roof holds. Mostly.
The puddles will be lakes if this keeps up.
Wet feet, wet back, wet mood.
Rain is only water from above. That's what I tell myself.
With a sky like that, anyone sensible stays inside.
Count the seconds after the flash. Then you know how close it is.
Let's hope nothing burns tonight.
A sky like this makes even me talkative.
Clear morning, clear head.
Look how red the sky is turning. Tomorrow stays dry.
Weeds. Always these weeds.
A pumpkin doesn't grow faster if you stare at it. I've tried.
Beetroot, potatoes, wheat - in that order, or it comes to nothing.
My hoe and I, we go back a long way.
Today the sky does my work for me.
Field tended, tools away. A good day.
Letters are the best thing that ever happened to us.
I have an enchantment you might like.
Careful with that candle, yes? Paper holds a grudge.
Early morning is the best time to read. No noise.
Some things can't be bought. But much can be traded.
I collect what others throw away. You never know.
Lapis, redstone, a spider eye... don't ask further.
At this hour the signs are clearest.
Nobody goes into a cave without armour. Nobody who comes back.
Chain, iron, diamond - each at its price.
An axe is more honest than a sword. But a sword sells better.
I grind, I hammer, I keep quiet. That's how I like it.
Bring me your tools, I'll make something of them.
Durability, efficiency, fortune. Which will it be?
The lake looks calm. Under the water it never is.
A bucket of fish, and you're the most popular soul in the village.
They bite better in the rain. Don't ask, just believe it.
Arrows, a bow, a bit of flint. That's all it takes.
I've yet to see a skeleton's bow better than mine.
Shears sharpened, sheep calm. A good day.
Red, blue, yellow - whatever you like, I'll dye it for you.
Cooked tastes better than raw. Remember that.
I've got rabbit, I've got chicken, I've got time.
Leather takes patience and a strong stomach.
A saddle? I have one. It'll cost you.
Stone becomes brick, brick becomes home.
Build crooked, live crooked.
A blank patch on the map is an invitation.
If you find a shipwreck, tell me. I pay well for good maps.
I have a trade! ...No? Really not? Heh-heh.
The librarian says I should learn to read. I say: what for?
Heh-heh. I'll just do as I please.
A workstation, any workstation. I'm not fussy.
If there were an anvil here, I'd be a smith. Instantly.
I am looking around. Really.
Buy now, it's gone tomorrow. So am I.
Two llamas, one sack, the whole world. Enough for me.
Do you know where the nearest road north runs?
Everything you see here comes from somewhere you've never been.
Early start, early arrival. Buying anything?
I'll wait here in this weather. We can trade in the meantime.
The nights here are as cold as the days are hot.
Cactus, sand, sun. Not much of a selection.
Flat, friendly, fertile. I want nothing more.
When a storm comes, you see it an hour ahead out here.
Wood enough for ten houses. And mushrooms for the soup.
Sweet berries on every corner here. And wolves.
Cold, but honest. That's how it is here.
These old pines stood here before the village did.
My toes have given up on me.
When it snows, everything goes quiet. I like that.
Everything here has turned to ice. Even the sounds.
At night there are eyes glowing in the water here. Stay on the path.
Slime, vines, frogs. It's an acquired taste.
Always damp, always warm, always a rustle somewhere.
Watch where you step. The ground here isn't always ground.
The bamboo grows faster than I can look.
Acacias grow crooked and stubborn. I like that.
Sand, stone and not a soul. Who lives here by choice?
Sand in your shoes, but who's complaining.
Somewhere out there are villages under the water. That's what they tell me.
The river brings everything past eventually. News included.
Only stones and water. No room for a field.
No monsters here. I don't know why, but I like it.
Pink as far as you can see. It softens a person.
Do you hear the bees? That's the finest work of all.
If I take a bunch home, nobody will notice. Will they?
Birch wood is bright and friendly. Like a village ought to be.
Stay away from the big houses around here. I mean it.
Frogs everywhere. I like them, but they never stop.
No hat lasts long here.
Goats. They'll shove you off if you don't watch out.
The firs carry their snow like a burden. Lovely sight.
Who built this? And why?
Mind your head. Those points come down sometimes.
Moss, water, light from the vines. A wonder down here.
Don't make a sound. Not one.
Red trees that aren't trees. Nothing here is what it seems.
Everything here is blue and wrong.
Those faces in the sand... I saw nothing.
Ash in the air, lava underfoot. Wonderful.
I hear water. And something else.
Have you got a torch? Please say yes.
I want to go home. Now.
Where's the ground? Where's the sky? Where am I?
If you go in there, come back out again.
No. No, no. I'm not going in there with you.
A loaf... would anyone have a loaf of bread?
I'm a villager, not a punching bag!
If the iron one sees that, you've got a problem.
Show me what you've got. I've got time.
Emeralds will get you almost anything here. Almost.
Everything is coming easy to me today!
Nobody missed me today. Does that show?
Move along. Nothing to see here.
Sometimes I picture this village with a tower. A really tall one.
When nobody is looking - are we still here?
As long as someone is sowing, nothing is lost.
My trade is old and it is good. Nobody can take that from me.
I lock up three times at night. Twice would do, I know.
Ask me something. Anything. Please.
I left a flower for her. She didn't notice.
I'm tired to the bone. But work is work.
Thank you for stopping by. Truly.
Weather like this makes a person go quiet inside.
My house used to have one more wall.
Don't look at the tall ones. Just don't look at them.
The iron one gave me another flower today.
If you see a black banner: ring the bell and get inside.
They come at night, when there are too many of us. So they say.
If you see lava: don't swim. Just a tip.
Don't ever sleep in a bed down here. It ends badly.
Some people build a whole house in a day. Out of nothing! Mad.
When everyone sleeps, morning is suddenly here. Practical.
Those big horned brutes... once is enough for a lifetime.
You can come back, I hear. With an apple and a bit of luck.
Sixty-four. Always sixty-four. Don't ask me why.
Fly, you fools! ...Ah. We can't fly.
They say there's a school for this sort of thing. For enchanting, I mean.
I'll be back. I have to be, I live here.
Someone was standing in the snow outside the house. I hope it was the wind.
Don't go in the water. Don't ask, just don't.
Shaken, not stirred. The potion, I mean.
Second breakfast isn't a thing here. I asked.
Where my treasure is? Ask the cartographer.
Out here, no one can hear us. No one at all.
Home. There's no place like it.
I used to just say 'ehh'. Now suddenly I'm speaking in whole sentences. Strange.
Sometimes I wonder who actually paved these paths.
I think I'll count how many chests are in the village today.
The bell sounded different today. Or am I imagining it?
A good day starts with a full cellar.
I should really tidy up more often. I tell myself that every day.
Who invented beds in the first place? Good person, whoever they were.
Some days are made for talking. Today's one of them.
I think my neighbour has more emeralds than he lets on.
Without the paths I'd constantly get lost. Well, more than I already do.
A good trade takes patience. And a fat purse.
I've never once seen a rounded edge. Does that even exist?
Even the clouds here have corners. Practical, really.
I only ever walk in straight lines. Curves are a mystery to me.
Life finds a way, they say. Rarely, in my case.
If this place is haunted, I know exactly who you'd need to call.
Someday I want to get so fast I outrun time itself.
I think my power today is well beyond anything measurable.
I dream of becoming king of all trade routes. Just once, at least.
Sometimes I think a little forest spirit is watching me from the trees.
I wonder if we lose our memories every time the village restarts.
Sometimes the world flickers for a moment. Have you noticed that too?
If I stand here too long, I'll probably start growing right along with it.
Even your thoughts move slower down here.
This colour... I think I miss green.
I think my toes have already turned to ice.
Standing next to these trees, I feel tiny.
The rushing water calms me more than I'd like to admit.
Every step here drags at me, like the ground wants to keep me.
Not the comfiest place to think, but it'll do.
So blue out here - I could almost forget where I am.
I hope you believe in the heart of the cards too.
You can tell a villager's harvest by the look of their nose.
I think spring's coming earlier than usual this year.
Every day starts the same: door open, sun in, and off we go.
Sometimes I wish the days were just a little longer.
I caught my reflection in the well this morning. Unsettlingly familiar.
There are worse places than this. I just haven't found one yet.
When I grow up... ah, right, I already have.
Everyone knows everyone here. Sometimes that's a blessing, sometimes not.
I think I forgot something important yesterday. It'll come back to me.
Peace and quiet is just another word for 'not interrupted yet'.
I like the sound of the village going quiet.
What do you think of a fresh start? Generally speaking.
Sometimes I think this village grows faster than I can keep count.
I counted the birds this morning. Stopped at seven.
Everyone needs a purpose. Mine's apparently standing around here.
I don't think I'll ever understand why time moves so fast.
A little chaos is part of it. Otherwise it'd be boring.
You don't have to understand everything to be content.
I'm already looking forward to tomorrow. No particular reason.
If I'm honest, I sometimes miss being alone. Just for a moment.
I think the weather's got something planned for me today.
Small things make the day. A warm loaf of bread, for instance.
I could've sworn there was a fence here yesterday.
You don't get wiser, just older. Mostly, anyway.
I collect stories. Sadly, no one's told me a good one yet.
When it's quiet, I listen to myself think.
I think everyone here has a secret. I'm not telling you mine.
In the end, all that matters is going to bed with a full stomach.
I like days where nothing special happens. They're underrated.
Sometimes I wonder if other villages talk just like we do.
I think I need a conversation that isn't about trading, for once.
Trust has to be earned. Emeralds alone won't quite cut it.
I once counted how many times a day I say 'Hm'. Too many.
A village without laughter is just a pile of houses.
I think my best idea came to me while doing absolutely nothing.
You should say thank you more often. Even for small things.
I love the moment right before sunrise the most.
If everyone helps a little, it gets easier for everyone in the end.
I think I sometimes talk to myself more than to anyone else.
What doesn't work today might work tomorrow. Or the day after.
At the end of the day, a solid roof overhead is worth a lot.
My cat sleeps on the emerald chest all day. At least she's guarding something.
The cows moo louder in the morning than our bell. No wonder I'm up early.
I've never had to count sheep to fall asleep. One's enough with this racket.
The pigs in the pen look more content than most of us.
Somehow that one chicken lays more eggs than all the others combined. Better not to ask how.
My horse has more personality than half the neighbours. And fewer opinions.
The hunter's tamed wolf follows him everywhere. I wish my cat was half that loyal.
Those rabbits multiply faster than I can keep count.
I like the bees. As long as I keep my distance.
Sometimes I spot a fox at the edge of the forest. It looks just as suspicious as I feel.
The trader's llamas spit more than they trade.
A parrot copied my voice the other day. Unsettlingly good, I have to admit.
I never fall asleep until I've checked the door twice. With what prowls the village at night, you learn to.
Sometimes I hear that hiss right before the bang. I just run first and ask why later.
The enchanting table mutters to itself at night. No idea what it's saying, but it sounds important.
A diamond sparkles brighter than any candle. Still, I'd rather trade it for bread.
Redstone dust gets everywhere in my pockets. I swear my trousers glow at night by now.
Whoever invented TNT, I hope they don't live next door to me.
An empty bucket is surprisingly useful. A full one even more so, until it tips over.
My compass always points back to the village. Handy, in case I ever forget where I live.
There's more paper than actual land on my map. Still finds me home somehow.
Some folks fly through the air with those wings. I'll stick to the ground, thanks.
I heard there's a little statue that keeps you from dying. Sounds like sorcery to me.
Those pearls from the End unsettle me. Who willingly throws themselves somewhere else?
A bed is about the best thing you can own. After emeralds, of course.
That anvil makes more noise than it's worth sometimes, if you ask me.
A good bow saves you a lot of unpleasant walks.
Holding a shield makes you feel twice as brave. Even when you really aren't.
My fishing rod caught an old boot the other day. At least it wasn't a monster.
Obsidian is harder than any head in this village. And that's saying something.
Netherite's supposed to come from the Nether. Explains the price, I suppose.
A whole cake for one person? That's almost rude how much it is.
A golden apple probably tastes like nothing at all. At least it shines nicely.
My clock never shows the right time, but at least it spins reliably.
A firework in the night sky, and for a moment you forget it's dangerous out there.
Coal isn't pretty, but without it the furnace stays cold.
Iron is honest. No shine, but you can rely on it.
Gold looks nice, but it's barely good for anything sensible. Typical.
You only find diamonds if you dig deep enough. And have patience.
Emeralds matter more to me than any other stone. Obvious reasons.
Lapis lazuli is bluer than the sky on a good day.
Mine some redstone and you usually come back up dusted red.
Copper turns green over time. Just like me, if I stand in the sun too long.
Those purple crystals in the cave almost hum if you listen closely.
Quartz from the Nether is brighter than anything I know up here.
I planted an oak sapling. In a hundred years, that'll be a proper tree.
Sugar cane grows by the water almost on its own. Like it's trying to show me something.
A cactus out front at least keeps unwanted visitors away.
Mushrooms in the shade grow faster than any excuse.
The turtles on the beach never seem to rush. Maybe I should take a page from their book.
The squids in the river look like they've got all the time in the world.
Sometimes I hear bats flutter at night. Doesn't bother me, as long as they stay outside.
A spider in the corner bothers me less than the ones that get bigger at night.
Those little pink water creatures underground are cuter than you'd expect.
The wild ocelots in the jungle won't let you near them. Proud animals.
Without my workstation I feel almost naked. Professionally speaking.
The iron golem looks after us better than we ever could ourselves.
When the bell rings, we all know: inside, door shut.
Some of us used to be... different. We don't talk about it.
A village without trade is like a house without a roof.
I don't trade the same with everyone. Some have simply earned the trust.
Reputation is everything here. Ruin it once, and it's remembered.
We get new little ones here faster than we can build beds. Almost embarrassing.
Everyone here has their spot in the village. Mine's apparently next to the well.
If a zombie gets one of us, it turns ugly. And green.
A creeper makes no sound until it's too late. That's why I always look twice.
We usually smell zombies before we see them. Not a nice advantage to have.
Skeletons shoot from a distance. Cowards, if you ask me.
Never look an enderman in the eyes. That's what I was told, not what I tried.
The witch by the swamp brews odd things. I'd rather keep my distance.
The anvil's already sparked three times today. Good day for armour.
I'd rather forge chestplates than tools. More honour in it.
My hands are more calloused from the hammer than any leather.
A good set of armour outlasts most promises.
The smell of hot iron is just part of my day.
Without me, it'd just be raw meat around here. Thankless work, but someone's got to do it.
My chopping block has seen more than I care to admit.
Fresh meat always sells better than old. Who would've guessed.
I smell like smoke all day long. Doesn't seem to bother my customers.
A good cut is the difference between a meal and a mess.
I draw maps of places I've never actually been. Ironic, isn't it?
My paper stock runs out faster than I can restock it.
A good map doesn't lie. Mostly, anyway.
I once tried to draw our village. It looked like a potato field.
Compass and quill are more sacred to me than most tools here.
The brewing stand's been bubbling for hours. Patience is part of the craft.
I mix potions, not miracles. Even if it looks that way sometimes.
A good potion needs the right ingredient and even more time to rest.
Nether wart smells worse than it tastes. Good thing you don't drink it raw.
My robe has more stains than any recipe book.
My hoe and I have seen more fields than most people here have seen beds.
Rain is to me what emeralds are to others.
